entries.title: regenerate package-lock.json for v0.15.0
entries.body:
The platform packages for v0.15.0 are on the registry now, so `package-lock.json` can point at them. The release commit bumped the pins in `package.json` and the lockfile root, but it could not move the platform packages' `resolved` URLs and `integrity` hashes. Those belong to tarballs that exist only once `release.yml` has published them. Until now, `npm ci` on main and the `lint` job failed.

Generated by the `lockfile` job in `release.yml` with `npm install --package-lock-only --ignore-scripts`.
entries.author: github-actions[bot]

entries.title: record the parser run as built, quote NL2038 whole, and make a failed expect stop a parse path
entries.body:
WP33 §5.0 said the diagnostic for forbidden TypeScript "is the wrong one" and dated its table to 0.12.0, although R1's parser half (#292, #311, #313, #314, #315, #337) closed exactly that. The section now says what changed and from which release: 0.14.0 for every row of its table. It also says what the inventory really was: the 75 codes of the old "Retired at R6" parser section, plus `for...in`.

wp19's declared divergence 602 still called closing it "a parser rewrite, not a fix". Its two rows and the bullet on the 41 lost wordings keep their history and gain a forward note to the run that closed them.

LANGUAGE.md now quotes NL2038 as the compiler prints it, with the supported-types list, and AI.md marks the omitted tail with "…".

`.claude/selfhost.md` gains the convention #337's review kept finding: a parse path stops at its first failed `expect`. A malformed form must cost no more diagnostics than it did before the path existed. The parse-then-refuse bullet no longer points at the R6 section of `unreachable.txt`, which that run deleted.
entries.author: Amrit Kahlon

entries.title: export x509DerSignatureRS, and run P-256's Wycheproof cases through it
entries.body:
`nish/crypto/x509` already read a DER ECDSA-Sig-Value strictly, to verify a certificate's signature. It now exports that reader as `x509DerSignatureRS`, which returns the `r || s` that `nish/crypto/p256` takes, or `null` unless the input is exactly one minimal, positive pair below 2^256. That is the form a TLS `CertificateVerify` carries.

`tests/link/crypto_p256` read Wycheproof's DER signatures with a private copy of that parser. So 235 of the 310 invalid `ecdsa_secp256r1_sha256` cases were refused by test code rather than by the library, and nothing the library shipped was held to them. The suite now uses `x509DerSignatureRS` and the copy is deleted. The library refuses the same 235 and `p256Verify` the same 75, in both number profiles.

Closes #351.
entries.author: Amrit Kahlon

entries.title: refuse a duplicate type parameter and name the empty statement's rule
entries.body:
A type parameter list that names one parameter twice, `<T, T>`, used to compile: the registry had NL2302's `Duplicate type parameter` and nothing raised it. The pass 1 sweep now checks it at each type parameter, in source order, on a function, an arrow (including a module `const` bound to one), a method, a class and an interface. Because the check is in the sweep, a template nothing instantiates is refused too. There is one diagnostic per list, on the first repeat. A type alias's list is refused first by NL1054 in Phase 0.

The empty statement `;` in a body used to be refused with ``Unsupported statement `;` ``, which carried no code (NL0000). The fallback in the statement dispatch now names the syntax kind in NL2260's sentence, `Unsupported statement in Phase 1: EmptyStatement`. `;` stays refused, so the language does not change; only the sentence and its code do. A `;` in a template nothing instantiates still compiles, as it did in every release, because the rule is asked when a body is checked.

Both lines leave `tests/wordings/stage1_divergence.txt`, which is now empty of cases, and NL2302 leaves `unreachable.txt`. The uncoded backlog drops to 0, and `UNCODED_BACKLOG` in `tests/run.js` is lowered to match so it cannot grow back. No `.ll` golden moved.

Measured: scripts/bootstrap.sh --verify user time 1m42.7s on main vs 1m38.9s on the branch
Refs: #320, docs/LANGUAGE.md#generic-functions, docs/LANGUAGE.md#rejected-statements
Tests: tests/cases/reject_generic_duplicate_type_parameter, …_arrow, …_method, …_class, …_interface, …_template, …_triple, tests/cases/reject_stmt_empty, tests/wordings/nl2302_duplicate_type_parameter, tests/wordings/nl2260_empty_statement

Closes #320
entries.author: Amrit Kahlon

entries.title: export NISH_BOOTSTRAP from the session-start hook, so a session's npm test runs nish-cmp
entries.body:
Without `NISH_BOOTSTRAP`, `npm test` skips nish-cmp and the stage1 fuzz, which compare HEAD with the last release. In a fresh cloud session that was a third skip beside the two wasi ones, and the definition of done allows only those, so every agent had to work out by hand that this one was fine.

The session-start hook already fetches the last release into `build/seed/`. It now also exports that path as `NISH_BOOTSTRAP` through `CLAUDE_ENV_FILE`, and prints it with the tools it found. A value already set wins. CI is unchanged: its `test` job leaves the variable unset and runs nish-cmp as a job of its own, so the three-minute comparison is not run twice. `.claude/node.md` says what the variable does and where it comes from.

Closes #353.
entries.author: Amrit Kahlon

entries.title: type-check the interop declarations in one tsc program instead of eight spawns
entries.body: `npm test` spawned `tsc --noEmit --strict` once for each of the eight `.d.ts` files `--emit-dts` writes, about 2.4 s apiece and nearly all of it Node start-up, loading `typescript` and re-checking the default libs. `tests/typecheck.js` now runs tsc in the harness's own process with the options the CLI builds and the working directory the spawn had, and checks every file that cannot reach outside its own module in one program. A file that imports, references, or touches the global scope gets a program of its own, which is the old check. Each file keeps its own PASS line and its own diagnostic text, byte-identical to spawned tsc; a broken probe in the shared program pins the attribution. The six WP16 ambient `tsc -p` checks keep a program each but run in-process too.
metrics: the eight .d.ts checks 23.2 s -> 1.8 s on a shared 4-core box; CI's test job 9m49s -> 10m45s wall on the PR run, before the other speed-ups land (runner variance dominates)
tests: tests/run.js (the attribution probe and routing-table self-checks)
entries.author: Amrit Kahlon

entries.title: keep the compiler npm test built instead of linking it twice
entries.body: The `test` job linked `src/` with the seed into `build/nish` in its own step, and `npm test` then linked the same `src/` with the same seed again into `build/nish-test`. The two are the same build: same seed, entry, `speed` profile, `--link` path and runtime, differing only in how the entry path is spelled in each module's `source_filename`, and the binaries are byte-identical. The separate step is gone; after the suite passes, `cp build/nish-test build/nish` hands the binary the suite just tested to the smoke test, the cookbook check and the size report. `tests/run.js` is unchanged and still builds its own compiler on every run, so it never tests a stale one. The "golden cases, in Nish" job keeps its own link, since it has no suite to take one from.
metrics: removes the 30 s "Build the compiler with the seed" step from the test job (run 36610344594)
entries.author: Amrit Kahlon

entries.title: record what the WP34 crypto lane taught about goldens, provenance, measurements and PR bodies
entries.body:
Four rules, each from something that cost a review round or a re-run in the
K2–K6 crypto lane (#323):

- **`tests/self/goldens/checked.txt`** (`.claude/testing.md`). It conflicts
  whenever two open pull requests each add a `tests/cases` program. Resolve it
  by merging `main` and regenerating, as the last push before merging. One pull
  request needed four such merges.
- **Name the closest upstream** (`.claude/licensing.md`). When an algorithm has
  a well-known implementation, the pull request names it and says, function by
  function, whether the code follows its structure. Two slices claimed to be
  written from the specification when a function followed BearSSL or dudect.
- **`Measured:` states the figures** (CLAUDE.md). A trailer that pointed at the
  pull request body lost P-256's numbers from the changelog. Benchmarks vary
  their input and print a checksum, because one measurement came out twenty
  times too fast.
- **Read a pull request's body back after opening it** (CLAUDE.md), and delete
  any session-link footer the platform appended, which `pr-body.yml` refuses.
entries.author: Amrit Kahlon

entries.title: refuse import.meta by its rule, not NL0001
entries.body:
`import.meta` is valid TypeScript, an ES2020 meta-property, and Nish has no module object for it to name. Until now it failed as a cascade of syntax errors: `const u = import.meta` in a body cost five NL0001s, a top-level `const u = import.meta.url` four, and a bare `import.meta;` two. It is now one diagnostic that states the rule (NL1060): `` `import.meta` is forbidden in Nish (a module has no runtime object; resolve paths at compile time) ``.

The parser reads `import.meta` wherever an operand stands, in the shape a dynamic `import(…)` already has: an `N_MEMBER` named `meta` whose receiver is the IDENT `import`. A member access or a call after it (`import.meta.url`, `import.meta.env.MODE`, `import.meta.resolve("./lib")`) is read through and costs nothing extra. Phase 0 refuses it.

Only `.meta` opens the form. `import.foo` stays the syntax error it was, with the same count as before, and no truncation costs more than it did. `meta` stays an ordinary name everywhere else, and `tests/parser/names-meta.ts` pins those readings, which the release compiles to the same bytes. No `.ll` golden moved, and the compiler still rebuilds itself to a fixed point.

Measured: scripts/bootstrap.sh --verify user time 1m31.9s on main (fcd2253) vs 1m31.4s on the branch
Refs: #342, docs/LANGUAGE.md#expressions
Tests: tests/cases/reject_import_meta, tests/cases/reject_import_meta_call, tests/wordings/nl1060_import_meta.ts, tests/parser/names-meta.ts

Closes #342
entries.author: Amrit Kahlon

entries.title: delegate the test job's fixed point to the bootstrap row
entries.body: The largest single check in the `test` job's `npm test` was `src/ compiles src/: the bootstrap reaches a fixed point`, which asserts `IR(stage1) == IR(stage2)` and `stage3 == stage2`. The `bootstrap (x86_64-linux)` row of the same workflow already asserts both through `scripts/bootstrap.sh --verify`, with the same seed, profile and platform, in parallel. The `test` job now passes `--delegate-fixed-point`, and when that flag is given under `GITHUB_ACTIONS` on a host with a seed target, `tests/run.js` records the check as **delegated** — a third count beside passed and skipped, with a note naming the job that proves it — rather than running it a second time. Skips are counted as before, so a delegation never reads as a degraded run. A local `npm test` still runs the fixed point, and a new check fails if `ci.yml` ever passes the flag while the bootstrap job has lost `needs: seeds` or `bootstrap.sh --verify`.
metrics: the fixed-point check took about 80 s of the test job on run 36610344594; the test job on this PR's final run took 8m58s
entries.author: Amrit Kahlon

entries.title: audit and harden ChaCha20-Poly1305 and AES-GCM
entries.body:
A security audit of `nish/crypto/chacha20poly1305` and `nish/crypto/aes`, recorded in `docs/security/crypto-aead.md`. Both Opens already computed the whole tag over the received ciphertext and compared it in constant time before any plaintext existed; no counter could wrap within an array-sized message.

Three Low findings, all fixed:

- An `AesKey` built or edited by hand with a zero hash subkey made `aesGcmOpen` accept any ciphertext carrying one valid tag. The tag check now folds in a constant-time H ≠ 0 mask, so such a key opens nothing.
- An `AesKey` whose round count disagrees with its round keys panicked on an index; every AES entry point now answers `null` for it.
- Seal and Open check the ChaCha20 block-counter bound and SP 800-38D's 2^32 − 2 block limit explicitly rather than relying on `i32` array lengths.

All 325 Wycheproof ChaCha20-Poly1305 vectors and the 103 AES-192 GCM vectors (which `aesKey` must refuse) now run in both number modes.
entries.author: Amrit Kahlon

entries.title: run each golden case's whole pipeline in parallel
entries.body: The `tests/cases/` corpus already compiled `defaultJobs()` cases at a time, but everything after the compile — the portability recompile, the golden comparison, `llvm-as`, the link and the native run — ran one case at a time. Each case now runs from compile to native run as one job in the existing `tests/pool.js` pool. A job records its checks, `WROTE` lines and link specimen instead of printing them, and the main loop replays them in corpus order as soon as every earlier case has finished, so the log, the counts and the failure detail are unchanged and still stream. The native programs keep a single lane, because `io_nish_import` and `io_nish_import_global` share a data file they must keep; the `runtime objects:` specimen stays the first case in corpus order. `UPDATE_GOLDENS=1` behaves as before.
metrics: the corpus section 68 s -> 21-25 s on a 4-core box; the CI test job 9m49s (run 36610344594) -> 8m36s on this PR's final run, with #367, #368 and #370 already on main
entries.author: Amrit Kahlon

entries.title: audit and harden SHA-2, HMAC, HKDF, ct and base64url
entries.body:
A security audit of `nish/crypto`'s SHA-2 hashes, HMAC, HKDF, `timingSafeEqual` and base64url, recorded in `docs/security/crypto-k1.md`.

The bit-length counters were sound; the bug was one layer up. Under `--number-mode f64` an array's length is exact, but every whole-buffer entry point narrowed it with `toI32`, which saturates at 2^31 − 1. Each guard now compares the length as the `number` it is:

- One-shot `sha256`, `sha384`, `sha512`, `hmacSha256` and `hmacSha384` panic on an array longer than 2^31 − 1 bytes, which they used to hash as its prefix: a collision and a MAC forgery (High).
- `timingSafeEqual` no longer answers `true` for arrays of 2^31 and 2^31 − 1 bytes (High).
- `base64urlDecode` refuses an over-long text instead of decoding its prefix, and `hkdfExpand*` refuses an over-long `info` and, per RFC 5869 §2.3, a PRK shorter than HashLen (Low).

`timingSafeEqual`, `timingSafeEqualAt` and base64url's character maps are now held to the disassembly check by new `ct_asm_k1_*` fixtures.

One High finding remains open outside this module: under `--number-mode i32`, `.length` truncates an array's length to 32 bits, so a program in that mode must not pass these functions an array of 2^31 bytes or more until the compiler refuses it.
entries.author: Amrit Kahlon

entries.title: audit and harden P-256 ECDSA and X25519
entries.body:
A security audit of `nish/crypto/p256` and `nish/crypto/x25519` against SEC 1, FIPS 186-4, RFC 6979 and RFC 7748, recorded in `docs/security/crypto-ecc.md`. It found no forgery, key recovery, panic, non-canonical accept or secret-dependent branch.

- `p256Verify` refuses an `r` or `s` of 0 or n or more, an off-curve or identity key, and a sum at the identity. `p256Sign` refuses a private key of 0 or n or more. The fiat-crypto port matches upstream `abe078c` statement for statement.
- High `s` is accepted: ECDSA is malleable by design. `p256Verify`'s doc now says so, and a test pins it.
- `x25519`'s doc no longer claims that TLS refuses an all-zero shared secret; no TLS module exists yet, so a caller has to make that check itself.

1,666 more Wycheproof cases now run in both number modes: `ecdsa_secp256r1_sha256_p1363`, `ecdsa_secp256r1_sha512`, `ecdsa_secp256r1_sha512_p1363` and `x25519_test`. The X25519 vectors have their own file and `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` row.
entries.author: Amrit Kahlon

entries.title: refuse computed keys and object spread by their rule, not NL0001
entries.body:
A computed key and object spread used to stop at the parser with `an object literal key must be a plain identifier`, followed by a cascade of further syntax errors (ten for `{ [k]: 1 }`, five for `{ ...a }`), so `--json` never named the rule. The parser now reads both into the node each resembles, and Phase 0 refuses each once, by its own rule:

- a computed name, in every container TypeScript allows it — an object literal (`{ [k]: 1 }`, `{ [k]() { } }`), a class (`[k]: i32`, `[Symbol.iterator]() { }`) and an interface (`[k]: i32`) — is `Computed property names are forbidden in Nish (member names are fixed at compile time)`, NL1041. `[Symbol.dispose]()` is still the one bracketed name read as a name. In a class and an interface, main answered NL0001 for every one of these.
- object spread, `{ ...a }`, is the `N_SPREAD` an array literal's `...a` already is, among the object's properties, and is `Object spread is forbidden in Nish (set each field by name)`, NL1061, a code of its own. NL1007 stays the `Object.<static>` rule.

NL1041 was shadowed by NL1007: the two fragments were the same length and NL1007 sorts first. The computed-key sentence no longer ends that way, and it and the spread sentence are now what `docs/LANGUAGE.md` quotes. Within one literal the first refused form in source order is the one reported.

A computed name cut short is one syntax error. Its member is abandoned, and an object literal skips the broken property to its `,` and parses the next one, so no truncation costs more diagnostics than on main, and most cost fewer (`{ [k]: 1, [` goes from 9 to 2).

The words stay names wherever TypeScript reads a name. A generated sweep of 24,368 programs gives IR byte-identical to main's for all 525 that main compiles, compiles none that main refuses, and agrees with the `typescript` parser on every one of the 12,347 files the parser oracle compares. No `.ll` golden moved, and the compiler still rebuilds itself to a fixed point.
metrics: scripts/bootstrap.sh --verify user time 1m39.2s on main vs 1m38.7s on the branch (seed 0.15.0); `{ [, b: 2 }` 1 diagnostic, as on main
entries.author: Amrit Kahlon

entries.title: audit and harden the DER, PEM and X.509 parsers
entries.body:
A security audit of `nish/crypto/x509` (the DER reader, the PEM codec, the key and certificate parsers, `x509VerifySignature` and `x509MintSelfSigned`), recorded in `docs/security/crypto-x509.md`. No input panicked, looped or allocated beyond its own size, and no edited input came back as a key, signature or certificate that passes for the original. Eight Low findings, six fixed:

- `pemToDer` decodes every block, whatever its label, and refuses the file if any block is malformed. A good key could hide beside a bad one before.
- `x509ParseCertificate` reads the `[1]`, `[2]` and `[3]` fields it used to skip. `[3]` must hold exactly one non-empty SEQUENCE, and both unique identifiers follow the DER BIT STRING grammar.
- `x509ParseP256PrivateKey` holds a PKCS#8 v1 key's outer public key to the key's own point, as it already did for SEC1.
- `x509MintSelfSigned` refuses a common name that is not well-formed UTF-8 or that holds a NUL.
- The docs say what the parsers do not check: they parse and do not validate, and extensions are neither checked nor exposed.

Still open: the mint takes its key and serial from the caller (they must come from `crypto.getRandomValues`), and private-key material is never wiped.

A fixed-seed corpus of 25,281 malformed inputs, derived from every valid fixture, now runs under `npm test`.
entries.author: Amrit Kahlon

entries.title: prove the constant-time checks catch what they claim
entries.author: Amrit Kahlon

entries.title: audit bounds-check elimination and emitted attributes
entries.body:
A security audit of what the compiler proves away and what it promises LLVM, recorded in `docs/security/codegen.md`. The audit covered three things:

- every elimination rule in `src/bounds.ts`, each run against a counter-program;
- every attribute `src/attributes.ts` and `src/escape.ts` emit, checked against its proof and `opt -O2`;
- the thread rules, run under ThreadSanitizer.

Fixed:

- `new Array<T>(n)` checks an `i64`, `u64` or float length (a `u32` one under i32 mode) before it allocates. `n * sizeof(T)` can no longer wrap to an empty block behind a huge header, and a NaN never reaches `fptosi`. Those cases segfaulted before (High).
- An array never grows past 2^31 − 1 elements, in either number mode, so an i32-mode `.length` cannot truncate a grown array (High).
- An element of a `readdirSync` listing now keeps the listing alive, so neither a function's arena scope nor a loop pass releases a name it hands out (High).
- `orReturn` between a `scope()`'s first `spawn` and its join is refused (NL2394). It returned without joining, leaving a task writing into released memory (High).
- A task argument read out of a variable now hands that variable on, so a store into it before the join is refused (Medium).

Still open, outside this change: under `--number-mode i32`, an array or string longer than 2^31 − 1 that arrives from `readFileBytesSync`, `readFileSync`, `join` or concatenation has a negative `.length`, which bounds-check elimination trusts. Two Medium findings are also open: a negative `new Array` length wraps the inline allocator, and `willreturn` is inferred through recursion.
metrics: `runtime.c` .text at -Oz 3,551 bytes (budget 3,584); every map benchmark row within +0.100%
entries.author: Amrit Kahlon

entries.title: audit nish run's cache and the compiler's file and process handling
entries.body:
This change audits `nish run`'s cache and the compiler's package-root lookup, toolchain spawns and output paths. It fixes what it found inside the CLI. The record is `docs/security/cli.md`.

- **A compiler outside its package no longer takes the working directory as its package root** (CLI-2, High). Before, `--link` would run the checkout's own `./scripts/build.sh`, and `nish/<module>` was compiled from `./std/`, so compiling someone else's checkout executed their script. `.` is now a candidate only when the compiler's real path is inside it, and `libraryRoot` never reads `nish/<module>` from the working directory.
- **`nish run key.ts` works** (CLI-1). The binary is now `key.bin`, so the cache key no longer overwrites it.
- **The cache is private and hard to poison:**
  - A relative `XDG_CACHE_HOME`/`HOME` is ignored (CLI-3).
  - The cache root is made `0700`, and a run is refused if that fails (CLI-4).
  - The entry's key is emptied before the binary is moved in (CLI-5).
  - `mv`/`rm` take `--`.
- A cache root that cannot be created is reported as such, not as a failed chmod (CLI-10).

Still open:
- CLI-6, writes that follow a symlink, is fixed in the runtime stage.
- CLI-7 and CLI-9 wait on the `lstat`/`access` primitives reaching a release.
- CLI-8 is the non-cryptographic entry name.
entries.author: Amrit Kahlon

entries.title: audit the C runtime for memory safety and OS misuse
entries.body:
A security audit of the C and wasm runtimes, recorded in `docs/security/runtime.md`. It checked:
- every size computation for overflow;
- every length handed back against 2^31 - 1;
- every path, name and argument given an embedded NUL;
- every file the runtime creates against a planted symbolic link;
- the socket buffers against the kernel's contract;
- the thread and signal code for races.

Fixed:

- **File reads (High, the runtime half of CG-3).** `readFileSync`, `readFileSyncOrNull` and `readFileBytesSync` treat a file longer than 2^31 - 1 bytes as unreadable. Before, its `length` read back negative under i32 mode and bounds-check elimination trusted it, so a sparse file was enough for an unchecked out-of-bounds read.
- **String concatenation (High).** Concatenation past 2^31 - 1 bytes fails as an allocation does.
- **NUL in a path (Medium).** A path, environment name or spawn argument holding a NUL names nothing. Before, `"README.md\0.txt"` passed a `.txt` check and opened `README.md`. The check is now one `nish_cpath` in `nish.h`.
- **Symbolic links (Medium, CLI-6).** `writeFileSync`, `appendFileSync` and `spawnSyncTo` refuse a symbolic link as the last component, so a link planted at `file.ll` can no longer make `nish file.ts` overwrite another file. `writeFileSync("/dev/stdout", …)` now fails on Linux; use `console.log` or `write`.
- **Directory listing (Medium).** `readdirSync` sorts with a heapsort.
- **Low findings:**
  - `udpRecvFrom` writes zeros, not uninitialised stack, when the socket reports no sender.
  - The wasm arena traps on a wrapped offset or a page count past 32 bits.
  - Both `nish_alloc_array`s refuse a length past 2^31 - 1 (CG-9).
  - `nish_parallel_range` no longer overflows a signed chunk count.

Each limit is pinned at exactly 2^31 - 1 as well as past it, without committing the memory.

Added for a later `src/` change: `nish_lstat_owner_mode`, `nish_euid` and `nish_is_executable` (CLI-7, CLI-9). Still open: `join` can exceed 2^31 - 1 (in `src/`, #382), and four Low findings (RT-10 to RT-13) recorded in the document.
metrics: readdirSync of 100,000 names 12.5 s -> 0.071 s (2,507,163,583 -> 3,019,323 compares); no runtime .text ceiling raised
entries.author: Amrit Kahlon

entries.title: audit install, launcher, seed fetch and release workflows
entries.body:
An audit of the distribution path, recorded in `docs/security/supply-chain.md`. It covers `install.sh`, the launcher and packaging, the seed fetch, all six workflows and the WASI host.

**Nothing downloaded is now unpacked or run before its SHA-256 matches** (SC-1..SC-3, Critical). Before, `install.sh` downloaded a release tarball, unpacked it and ran it with no checksum. The session hook, CI and the release job's `binaries` all got their seed that way, or through a bare `gh release download`.
- The 47 tarballs up to 0.15.0 are pinned in `install.sh`.
- `release.yml` now attaches a `SHA256SUMS` that later releases are checked against, and the npm job checks every package against the release job's sums before publishing.
- With no pinned digest and no `SHA256SUMS` line, nothing installs.
- CI takes every seed through `scripts/fetch-seed.sh`.

**CI seed rows refuse another platform's seed.** Each `bootstrap`/`nish-cmp` row passes its `matrix.seed.tarball` as `install.sh --expect-tarball`. The name must be exactly `nish-<dotted-integer version>-<asset>.tar.gz` for this machine's asset, so a runner label that drifts to other hardware fails instead of going green under the old row's name. With no version given, a malformed or mismatched name is refused before any request (SC-19..SC-26).

**The workflows:**
- no `${{ }}` is spliced into a `run:` script, and every `env:` key is upper case;
- every action is pinned to a commit SHA;
- the release job's write token is kept out of `.git/config`;
- npm is installed at an exact version in the `id-token: write` job.

Triggers and permissions are unchanged.

**The WASI host and the installer:**
- `web/wasi.mjs`'s `random_get` fails closed (`ENOSYS`) with no CSPRNG, instead of falling back to `Math.random` (SC-4, Medium). It fills requests past 64 KiB and refuses a range outside memory.
- `install.sh` validates the version, quotes the path its wrapper bakes in, and refuses to replace or uninstall a directory that is not an install.

Still open:
- SC-16, releases are mutable: turn on immutable releases in the repository settings.
- SC-17, `curl | sh` runs the script itself unverified; this is accepted.
entries.author: Amrit Kahlon

entries.title: add SECURITY.md and the audit index
entries.author: Amrit Kahlon
